House probe eyed amid SOCOTECO II–Ignite Power controversy
ph.description: A ranking House member is seeking a congressional inquiry on proposed joint venture between South Cotabato II Electric Cooperative Inc. (SOCOTECO II) and Ignite Power and Energy Corporation (Ignite). General Santos City lone district Rep. Shirlyn Bañas-Nograles, vice chairperson of the Committee on Nuclear Energy, introduced House Resolution (HR) No. 1401 for this purpose. Filed in the House of Representatives last Aug. 27, the measure directs the House Committee on Energy to conduct an investigation, in aid of legislation, into the Conditional Joint Venture Agreement (CJVA) between SOCOTECO II and Ignite. The resolution, pending first reading, seeks to determine whether the proposed arrangement complies with existing laws, rules and regulations, while examining issues of transparency, accountability and the prudent stewardship of cooperative assets. It also calls for an assessment of how the agreement could affect the rights and economic interests of the government and SOCOTECO II’s member-consumer-owners (MCOs). HR No. 1401 comes with "the end in view of determining compliance with existing laws, rules, and regulations; ensuring transparency, accountability, and the prudent stewardship of cooperative assets; protecting the rights and economic interests of the government and the member-consumer-owners; and strengthening the governance and regulation of joint venture arrangements involving electric cooperatives". Bañas-Nograles' initiative comes as opposition to the proposed partnership continues to grow. The Social Action Center of the Diocese of Marbel (SAC-Marbel) has raised questions regarding the process by which SOCOTECO II’s Board of Directors reportedly secured authority for the proposed joint venture. In a statement issued Aug. 20, the group alleged that Resolution No. 104 was declared adopted during the cooperative’s 43rd Annual General Membership Assembly on July 25 without a duly counted vote showing how many MCOs supported or rejected the measure. The concerns have placed the proposed joint venture under greater public and regulatory attention, particularly on questions involving the management and long-term stewardship of electric cooperative assets. Protesters from municipalities within the Diocese of Marbel carried banners calling for the proposed deal to be stopped and for the protection of the rights, resources and interests of SOCOTECO II’s member-consumer-owners. CARACAS, Venezuela , Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The United States Departments of State and War have reached an historic deal with North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to significantly expand oil production in Venezuela. As part of the deal, NABEP will have operating control of the business, with the United States Government holding rights to a 35% stake in the company, alongside preferential access to 20% of the company's production at cost. President Donald J. Trump announced the agreement on Truth Social as "the biggest oil deal in world history" and is demonstrative of the U.S. and Venezuelan governments deepening collaboration in the Venezuelan oil sector, bringing jobs and fiscal stability for Venezuelans and lower prices at the pump for Americans. "Venezuela is blessed with an abundance of natural resources, hardworking people and untapped potential," said Alejandro Betancourt, CEO of NABEP. "This transaction will unleash that potential to the great benefit of both Venezuelans and Americans. We are grateful to President Donald J. Trump, Secretary Marco Rubio, Secretary Pete Hegseth, the United States Government, and to President Delcy Rodríguez and the Government of Venezuela, for their confidence in NABEP and their willingness to tackle this challenge with us. We look forward to pioneering a new and exciting path together." This new venture is expected to bring tens of millions of additional barrels of Venezuelan oil to the global marketplace, thousands of well-paid jobs to Venezuela, and billions in incremental investment and broader economic activity to drive growth in Venezuela's recovering economy. Through the right to purchase 20% of the oil produced at cost, this venture will also ultimately deliver billions in savings for American consumers and secure a stable and growing strategic supply of oil in the Western Hemisphere. Through billions in purchases of oil infrastructure and equipment from U.S. suppliers, NABEP will also support thousands of manufacturing jobs in the United States. Mr. Betancourt has been in the Venezuelan oil industry for more than 15 years with a consistent track record of success, most recently at the helm of NABEP, where he rapidly scaled the company's production from approximately 18,000 barrels per day to more than 200,000 barrels per day through roughly $1 billion in company-funded investment, making it the country's second-largest oil producer in just two years' time. Today, the company directly employs over 5,000 people and supports over 10,000 contractor employees across Venezuela. Following these transactions, NABEP now controls the rights to commercialize more than 65 billion barrels of P1 reserves in Venezuela. NABEP is seeking to rapidly expand its operations in Lake Maracaibo and the Orinoco Belt with the near-term goal of increasing production to more than 1 million barrels of oil per day. As it was announced, the program will involve nearly $100 billion in investment to increase production capacity and oil and gas infrastructure in Venezuela and will generate more than $209 billion in tax revenue for the Venezuelan state. In a statement posted to X immediately following the announcement, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "This deal is a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people. It demonstrates how President Trump's bold foreign policy is driving America First wins: securing stable reserves and low-cost oil in our Hemisphere and lowering gas prices here at home. For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy." ae.title: United States Government and North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) Reach Historic Deal to Develop Venezuela's Oil Sector
ae.description: The deal, made possible by strengthening relations between Venezuela and the United States, is expected to involve nearly $100 billion in investment to commercialize more than 65 billion barrels of P1 reserves in Venezuela. CARACAS, Venezuela , Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The United States Departments of State and War have reached an historic deal with North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to significantly expand oil production in Venezuela. As part of the deal, NABEP will have operating control of the business, with the United States Government holding rights to a 35% stake in the company, alongside preferential access to 20% of the company's production at cost. President Donald J. Trump announced the agreement on Truth Social as "the biggest oil deal in world history" and is demonstrative of the U.S. and Venezuelan governments deepening collaboration in the Venezuelan oil sector, bringing jobs and fiscal stability for Venezuelans and lower prices at the pump for Americans. "Venezuela is blessed with an abundance of natural resources, hardworking people and untapped potential," said Alejandro Betancourt, CEO of NABEP. "This transaction will unleash that potential to the great benefit of both Venezuelans and Americans. We are grateful to President Donald J. Trump, Secretary Marco Rubio, Secretary Pete Hegseth, the United States Government, and to President Delcy Rodríguez and the Government of Venezuela, for their confidence in NABEP and their willingness to tackle this challenge with us. We look forward to pioneering a new and exciting path together." This new venture is expected to bring tens of millions of additional barrels of Venezuelan oil to the global marketplace, thousands of well-paid jobs to Venezuela, and billions in incremental investment and broader economic activity to drive growth in Venezuela's recovering economy. Through the right to purchase 20% of the oil produced at cost, this venture will also ultimately deliver billions in savings for American consumers and secure a stable and growing strategic supply of oil in the Western Hemisphere. Through billions in purchases of oil infrastructure and equipment from U.S. suppliers, NABEP will also support thousands of manufacturing jobs in the United States. Mr. Betancourt has been in the Venezuelan oil industry for more than 15 years with a consistent track record of success, most recently at the helm of NABEP, where he rapidly scaled the company's production from approximately 18,000 barrels per day to more than 200,000 barrels per day through roughly $1 billion in company-funded investment, making it the country's second-largest oil producer in just two years' time. Today, the company directly employs over 5,000 people and supports over 10,000 contractor employees across Venezuela. Following these transactions, NABEP now controls the rights to commercialize more than 65 billion barrels of P1 reserves in Venezuela. NABEP is seeking to rapidly expand its operations in Lake Maracaibo and the Orinoco Belt with the near-term goal of increasing production to more than 1 million barrels of oil per day. As it was announced, the program will involve nearly $100 billion in investment to increase production capacity and oil and gas infrastructure in Venezuela and will generate more than $209 billion in tax revenue for the Venezuelan state. In a statement posted to X immediately following the announcement, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "This deal is a huge win for both the American and Venezuelan people. It demonstrates how President Trump's bold foreign policy is driving America First wins: securing stable reserves and low-cost oil in our Hemisphere and lowering gas prices here at home. For the Venezuelan people, this deal will bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs, and drive the reconstruction of Venezuela's economy." About North American Blue Energy Partners North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) is an independent oil exploration and production company operating in North and Latin America, with offices in Caracas, Maracaibo and Lechería. NABEP is committed to the responsible development of energy resources, the safety of its people, and the prosperity of the communities where it operates. www.nabep.net Media contact press@nabep.com

ae.title: Strait of Hormuz commodity vessel transits stay in single digits
ae.description: SINGAPORE: The number of ‌vessels sailing through the Strait of Hormuz was little changed on Monday compared with the weekend, hovering around five, preliminary ship-tracking data showed on Tuesday, below the 10-day average of ⁠around 14. Four of the vessels entered the strait and one exited, data from Kpler showed. Vessels that sail through the strait ‌with their transponders turned off are not included in the count. No liquid tankers were ‌among those sailing through the waterway on ‌Monday, the data showed. Of those that ‌entered, one was ‌an empty handy-sized gas tanker which reached the strait via the Iranian ‌route. The other three were laden dry ⁠bulk carriers. On Tuesday, a Saudi oil tanker was stopped while transiting through the southern corridor ⁠of the ⁠Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian media reports. Meanwhile, at the other chokepoint, the Bab-el Mandeb strait, ⁠the number of vessels transiting was at a three-day high of 27, Kpler data showed, with 14 entering and 13 exiting. Five of the 27 vessel transits ‌were either Aframax- or Suezmax-sized crude tankers, according to the data. None of the vessels that entered or exited were very large crude carriers or liquefied natural gas tankers.

iq.title: الذهب يتراجع مع ترقب بيانات الوظائف الأمريكية وتصاعد التوترات في الشرق الأوسط
iq.description: شفق نيوز - بغداد / أربيل تراجعت أسعار الذهب، اليوم الثلاثاء، مع ترقب المتداولين صدور بيانات رئيسية عن سوق العمل الأمريكية هذا الأسبوع، في وقت يراقب فيه المستثمرون تطورات التوترات في الشرق الأوسط وانعكاساتها على التضخم وأسعار الفائدة. وانخفض سعر الذهب الفوري بنسبة 0.3% إلى 4437.10 دولاراً للأونصة بحلول الساعة 02:35 بتوقيت غرينتش، بعدما سجل في الجلسة السابقة أدنى مستوى له منذ 19 أغسطس/آب. في المقابل، ارتفعت العقود الآجلة للذهب الأمريكي بنسبة 0.1% إلى 4485.30 دولاراً للأونصة. وينتظر المتعاملون هذا الأسبوع صدور مجموعة من البيانات الاقتصادية الأمريكية، تشمل فرص العمل المتاحة، وتقرير التوظيف الصادر عن شركة ADP، إلى جانب بيانات الوظائف غير الزراعية، بحثاً عن مؤشرات بشأن قوة سوق العمل ومسار أسعار الفائدة الأمريكية. وكان الذهب قد صعد إلى أعلى مستوى له في أكثر من ثلاثة أشهر الأسبوع الماضي، قبل أن يتراجع بأكثر من 3% يوم الجمعة عقب تصريحات رئيس مجلس الاحتياطي الفيدرالي كيفن وارش بشأن ضرورة التأكد من استمرار تراجع التضخم نحو مستهدف البنك المركزي البالغ 2%. وقال محلل الأسواق في شركة IG توني سيكامور إن الذهب تعرض لضغوط بفعل اللهجة المتشددة لوارش، إلى جانب التوترات الجديدة في مضيق هرمز التي دفعت أسعار النفط إلى الارتفاع وزادت توقعات التضخم. وفي أسواق المعادن النفيسة الأخرى، ارتفعت الفضة الفورية بنسبة 0.3% إلى 66.34 دولاراً للأونصة، وصعد البلاتين بنسبة 0.1% إلى 1793.03 دولاراً، بينما استقر البلاديوم عند 1356.75 دولاراً للأونصة.

iq.title: النفط يرتفع مع تجدد مخاطر الإمدادات وسط تصاعد القتال الأمريكي الإيراني
iq.description: شفق نيوز - بغداد / أربيل ارتفعت أسعار النفط، اليوم الثلاثاء، مع تجدد المخاوف من اضطراب إمدادات الخام من الشرق الأوسط، بالتزامن مع استئناف القتال بين الولايات المتحدة وإيران وتصاعد المخاطر المرتبطة بحركة الملاحة في مضيق هرمز. وارتفع خام برنت 56 سنتاً، أو 0.6%، إلى 91.05 دولاراً للبرميل، فيما صعد خام غرب تكساس الوسيط الأمريكي 83 سنتاً، أو 1%، إلى 86.59 دولاراً للبرميل. وجاءت المكاسب بعد ارتفاع برنت في الجلسة السابقة بنسبة 2.7%، بينما زاد الخام الأمريكي 2.8%، وسط مخاوف من اتساع نطاق الصراع وتأثيره على البنية التحتية للطاقة وحركة ناقلات النفط في الخليج. وأظهرت بيانات شركة Kpler انخفاض عدد سفن البضائع المرئية التي تعبر مضيق هرمز إلى خمس سفن يومياً خلال عطلة نهاية الأسبوع، في وقت لم تحقق جهود الوساطة التي تقودها قطر وعُمان لإعادة فتح المضيق تقدماً حتى الآن. ويكتسب المضيق أهمية كبيرة لسوق النفط العالمي، إذ كان يمر عبره قبل اندلاع الحرب نحو خُمس إمدادات النفط العالمية. وفي تطور يزيد مخاطر الشحن، أكدت وكالة عمليات التجارة البحرية في المملكة المتحدة أن ناقلة نفط تعرضت لإصابة بثلاثة مقذوفات أثناء إبحارها خارج مضيق هرمز، دون تسجيل إصابات أو أضرار بيئية.
